g.text: What block, node, element, scene, content and asset mean, and how they nest
Canvas: the Slate document (editor.children). It is the project.
Asset elements: top level, ahead of every scene
AssetElement, ASSET_TYPES, asset_*. Hidden voids, shown in the asset strip. One per type and name.
Scenes: top level, after the assets
Scene, isScene. A scene groups content. It is a block, not an element.
a zero-width lead leaf, then the prompt text.
the Slate document; it is the project
any Slate node: the editor, a block, a text leaf.
A graph node (GenerationNode) is separate: one
CanvasBlock: a scene or an element
Scene: a group of content; not an element
CanvasElement: content or an asset. Holds text and
ContentElement: an element inside a scene. It plays
AssetElement: an element ahead of the scenes
an element whose type names a connector:
every content type, asset_avatar and asset_voice
an asset with no connector: style, references
an asset_avatar and/or asset_voice sharing a name.
The narrator is the asset_voice named Narrator
Not on the canvas: the project store
Metadata is read by plugins, never a node.
